markdown_report:
**Selected direction: bounded, bidirectional activation patching in NextItNet.** At 10% research progress, prioritize a diagnostic requiring no retraining or architecture changes.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 9.38% supplied-negative reversal rate in the endpoint probe. This identifies training separation worth investigating, without establishing validation weakness. (2) Frequency-matched older substitutions are less disruptive than random substitutions in Movies and CDs. Their negative absolute margin changes do not establish harmful older history. (3) Earlier catalog audits failed because deterministic CUDA execution lacked its required workspace configuration. Numerical preflight must precede interpretation, and failures must remain missing measurements.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions define possible temporal dependencies [1]. Actual information use requires intervention evidence. (2) Corruption choice and measurement affect activation-patching conclusions [2]. Endpoint replacement and interior reordering should therefore remain separate experimental conditions. (3) Restoration and disruption answer different questions [3]. Testing both directions, with no-op and donor controls, provides stronger evidence than restoration alone.

These insights organize three directions: execution reliability, temporal mechanism localization, and candidate robustness. The framework separates what each direction can establish:

| Direction | Measurement | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Reliability | Repeated-score and no-op agreement | Does not establish recommendation quality |
| Temporal localization | Controlled activation-patch effects | Does not identify present user intent |
| Candidate robustness | Training-target ranks under alternative candidates | Does not replace pinned validation |

Three atomic proposals follow; scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty, where higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Proposal | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Numerical preflight with explicit abstention [4] | 2/6/2 | Original integration detail; reusable; small implementation | Established practice; no mechanism discovery; backend restoration needs care |
| Bidirectional block-output patching [1–3] | 5/7/4 | Useful NextItNet adaptation; localizes temporal effects; hooks suffice | Established method; diagnostic gains may not predict HR@10; donor alignment needs care |
| Repeated training-candidate stress test | 3/6/3 | Separates candidate sensitivity; supports sampling research; scoring API suffices | Familiar design; evaluator mismatch persists; exclusions require care |

**Chosen algorithm.** Freeze each category’s single model. Select at most 32 identifiable training users, one prefix each, and fixed diagnostic candidates. Separately reorder earlier occupied items while preserving the endpoint, or replace only the endpoint. At two prespecified residual blocks, exchange the original-readout activation between clean and corrupted runs in both directions. Compare target-margin and rank changes against identity patches and matched shuffled donors; aggregate within users before reporting paired uncertainty.

Preserve both diagnostic entry points and ModelView interfaces. Keep original nonpadding readout, model state, RNG state, padding masks, and candidates fixed; remove hooks in `finally`. Report failed controls explicitly. No predictor changes or extra fitted models are required. These are training diagnostics; only host four-category macro validation HR@10 selects models. No new experiment or measurement is claimed.

idea.description: Add a bounded, contract-gated bidirectional activation-patching probe to each category’s single frozen NextItNet model, separating endpoint sensitivity from earlier-history ordering sensitivity.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics show relative temporal sensitivity, but do not identify where the trained network carries that information. Bidirectional patches can test whether selected block activations restore or disrupt target ranking under specific input interventions, without treating older history as harmful or inferring unobserved user intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Use actual residual-block output tensors after auditing their layout and masking; do not assume a module name or tensor axis from metadata alone. Select two blocks by documented depth fractions, resolving to distinct existing blocks. Cache at most ten loader batches and select at most 32 uniquely identifiable users with one valid training prefix each using local seed 42. Exclude ambiguous identities with counts. Use the original final occupied index, never count-1. Candidate sets contain the aligned training target and up to 99 unique valid sampled alternatives; exclude padding, target collisions, and observed pre-target items, and disclose realized counts. These candidates are diagnostic and never reconstructed host validation candidates. Keep candidate IDs identical across every paired condition. Interior permutations preserve occupied positions, padding and endpoint; endpoint replacements exclude candidates and observed pre-target items. Each corruption has its own clean/corrupted comparison. Patch only the selected block's activation at the original readout position; label this restricted site explicitly because other positions and residual paths remain unpatched. Run clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption, each relative to its corresponding unpatched recipient. Include clean-to-clean and corrupted-to-corrupted identity patches. Shuffled donors must come from other selected users with matching occupied length and endpoint ID; mark controls unavailable when no donor exists. Report raw target-minus-best-alternative margins, target-rank changes, diagnostic HR@10 changes, valid user counts, and missing reasons. Use a disclosed descending-score/ascending-item-ID diagnostic tie rule. Avoid normalized restoration ratios when corruption effects approach zero. Bootstrap paired user records with local seed 42; intervals remain conditional on the checkpoint, selected users, candidates and interventions, with no simultaneous guarantees. Preflight finite values, repeat scoring and identity patches. Configure CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 in the host entry point before CUDA initialization if deterministic CUDA execution is requested; the adapter must record configuration and abstain on unsupported execution rather than silently relaxing settings. Preserve and restore module modes, RNG and backend settings; remove all hooks in finally. The interpretation prompt must include measured metrics and definitions and distinguish observations, hypotheses and unavailable evidence. Keep training, predictor writer and architecture unchanged. Preserve four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category. Preserve the host’s full-catalog unseen-item recommendation workflow for five training users per category. Record diagnostic runtime against the shared budget. This proposal supplies an implementation specification, not executed code or measured gains.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = capture_module_modes_rng_and_backend_settings(self.view.model)
        hooks = []
        metrics, definitions = initialize_results_with_explicit_missingness()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            events = identify_and_select_training_events(
                train_loader, self.view.user_train,
                max_batches=10, max_unique_users=32, seed=42)
            sites = audit_and_choose_two_residual_block_output_sites(self.view.model)
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for event in events:
                    last = largest_nonzero_index(event.sequence)
                    candidates = fixed_training_diagnostic_candidates(event, seed=42)
                    clean = capture_forward(event.sequence, sites, last, candidates)
                    require_finite_repeatable_scores_and_identity_patch_agreement(clean)
                    for kind in ['endpoint_preserving_interior_permutation',
                                 'candidate_disjoint_endpoint_replacement']:
                        edited = make_controlled_corruption(event, kind)
                        corrupt = capture_forward(edited, sites, last, candidates)
                        for site in sites:
                            restored = forward_with_temporary_patch(
                                recipient=edited, site=site, position=last,
                                donor_activation=clean.activation[site][last])
                            disrupted = forward_with_temporary_patch(
                                recipient=event.sequence, site=site, position=last,
                                donor_activation=corrupt.activation[site][last])
                            record_paired_scores_ranks_and_hits(
                                clean, corrupt, restored, disrupted, candidates)
                            run_identity_and_available_matched_donor_controls()
            summarize_valid_users_and_conditional_paired_bootstrap(seed=42)
        except DiagnosticContractError as error:
            mark_affected_summaries_missing(str(error))
        finally:
            remove_all_hooks(hooks)
            restore_module_modes_rng_and_backend_settings(state)
        return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return evidence_grounded_prompt(
        metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        scope='Training sensitivity; no validation or user-intent claims')

originality.positive: Adapts bidirectional activation patching to causal NextItNet blocks with separate endpoint and ordering interventions and explicit deployment contracts.
originality.negative: Activation patching and matched controls are established; this is a practical adaptation rather than a new attribution principle.

future_potential.positive: Could motivate precise, single-model temporal regularization experiments by identifying reproducible intervention-sensitive sites.
future_potential.negative: Localized training sensitivity may reflect memorization or redundant computation and need not predict validation HR@10 improvements.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires bounded inference and temporary hooks without retraining, architecture changes or predictor export changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Auditing block layouts, matching donors, restoring execution state and checking patch validity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal dilated convolution and residual architecture underlying the preserved model family.
limitations: Architectural receptive fields identify possible dependencies, not measured information use by a trained checkpoint.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines how corruption methods and evaluation metrics affect activation-patching conclusions.
limitations: Language-model findings do not establish the validity or effectiveness of the proposed NextItNet adaptation.

related_work.title: How to Use and Interpret Activation Patching
contributions: Explains distinctions between restoration and disruption interventions and their interpretation.
limitations: Intervention effects depend on the chosen corruption and patch site; component interactions limit isolated conclusions.

related_work.title: PyTorch deterministic algorithms documentation
contributions: Documents deterministic execution requirements and operations that can raise errors when those requirements are unmet.
limitations: Enabling deterministic algorithms alone does not guarantee complete reproducibility or invariance across numerical execution shapes.
